messages.subject: divide data frame to multiple histograms
parts:
I have a data frame which contains many columns, some of them I want to create a histogram from, some of them I want to use to divide to the histograms.
I'll try to explain through an example:
Lets say my data frame looks like this:

    F1    F2    C1    C2
1   1.1   2.1   1      2
2   1.2   2.0   2      3
3    0.9  3.4   1      3
4    0.9  3.4   2      4

I want to get  a list of lists such that
l[["a"]][["f"]] contains the histogram created from values of feature f (F1 or F2) that contain classifications from C1 and C2 (1,2,3,4)

The collection of rows to be counted in a histogram would be such that the classificaiton appears in ANY of the "C" columns.

so for example the histogram of "a"=2 and "f"=F1 would be something similar to hist(c(1.1,1.2,0.9)) and that of "a"= 4 and "f"=F2 would be hist(c(3.4))

I am not sure how to even begin such a thing other than to start doing nested for loops

messages.author: a305e65fa9dfb74d
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] divide data frame to multiple histograms
parts:
How about:

A<- matrix(c(1.1, 2.1, 1, 2, 1.2, 2.0, 2, 3, 0.9, 3.4, 1, 3, 0.9, 3.4, 2, 4) , byrow=TRUE, ncol=4)
colnames(A)<- c('F1', 'F2', 'C1', 'C2')
A<- as.data.frame(A)
my.subset<- function(a,f) subset(A, subset= C1==a | C2==a, select=f)
my.subset(2, "F1")
